scope: Twenty ordered reduction-route questions: ten new direct routes and ten downstream proposals; they share ten new task definitions, so this is not twenty independent complexity classifications. None is a proved new reduction.

circle.title: A Quasi-Polynomial Time Algorithm for 3-Coloring Circle Graphs
circle.finding: A quasipolynomial algorithm handles both ordinary and list three-coloring; polynomial-time solvability remains unresolved.

pt.title: List 3-Coloring in tame classes of graphs in quasipolynomial time
pt.finding: List three-coloring is polynomial for t at most seven and quasipolynomial for every fixed t. This does not settle unrestricted P8-free inputs.

2p4.title: On 3-Coloring of (2P4, C5)-Free Graphs
2p4.finding: The paper identifies P8-free and 2P4-free three-coloring as unresolved and solves only the additional C5-free restriction.

diameter.title: Algorithms and Almost Tight Results for 3-Colorability of Small Diameter Graphs
diameter.finding: The paper leaves polynomial-time three-coloring for arbitrary diameter-two graphs open.

diameter2025.title: 3-Colorings of Diameter 2 Graphs
diameter2025.locator: Abstract and Introduction, May 2025 undergraduate thesis
diameter2025.finding: This later thesis still treats the general diameter-two case as open; it is supporting status evidence, not a new complexity theorem.

p7.title: Sparse Induced Subgraphs in P7-Free Graphs of Bounded Clique Number
p7.finding: Polynomial algorithms cover bounded clique number, while the general path-free setting has quasipolynomial algorithms. The bounded-clique result does not settle arbitrary P7-free inputs.

box.title: On the Boxicity of Line Graphs and of Their Complements
box.finding: The authors leave boxicity-two recognition and interval completion for line graphs unresolved. Their algorithms for complements of line graphs do not solve these cases.

cpg.title: Resolving Two Open Problems of Planar B_k-CPG Recognition: k=0,1
cpg.finding: The zero- and one-bend planar cases are settled, while the two-bend case remains open. An endpoint gadget is identified as the missing component.

cook.title: The complexity of theorem-proving procedures
cook.locator: Polynomial computation-tableau construction; witness recovery by reading the accepting certificate
cook.finding: A polynomial verifier admits a polynomial SAT encoding. This general upper-bound route does not give an encoding into 2-SAT.

diameter2021.title: Faster 3-Coloring of Small-Diameter Graphs
diameter2021.finding: The diameter-two algorithm uses subexponential branching and 2-SAT subroutines; it does not provide a polynomial reduction for every input.

circle2024.title: On 3-Coloring Circle Graphs
circle2024.locator: Abstract; discussion of the failed auxiliary-coloring encoding
circle2024.finding: Earlier claimed polynomial algorithms contain counterexamples. Local 2-SAT constraints do not establish a correct global coloring algorithm.

tasks.label: Circle graph 3-coloring search
tasks.definition: Input: a simple graph with a chord-diagram representation. Return a proper at-most-three coloring, or NO-SOLUTION.
tasks.status: Open in cited sources; no resolution found in scoped search; independent status review pending
tasks.obstacle: The quasipolynomial algorithm is not a polynomial reduction to 2-SAT; its branching and global color consistency must be compressed.

tasks.label: Circle graph list 3-coloring search
tasks.definition: Input: a chord diagram and, for every vertex, a list contained in {1,2,3}. Return a proper list-respecting coloring, or NO-SOLUTION.
tasks.status: Open in cited sources; no resolution found in scoped search; independent status review pending
tasks.obstacle: List restrictions must survive the proposed encoding and a satisfying 2-CNF assignment must decode to a complete coloring.

tasks.label: P8-free graph 3-coloring search
tasks.definition: Input: an explicitly encoded simple graph promised to contain no induced eight-vertex path. Return a proper at-most-three coloring, or NO-SOLUTION.
tasks.status: Open in cited sources; no resolution found in scoped search; independent status review pending
tasks.obstacle: A polynomial-size global encoding is missing; the P7-free algorithm does not directly cover P8-free graphs.

tasks.label: P8-free graph list 3-coloring search
tasks.definition: Input: a P8-free graph and vertex lists contained in {1,2,3}. Return a proper list-respecting coloring, or NO-SOLUTION.
tasks.status: Open in cited sources; no resolution found in scoped search; independent status review pending
tasks.obstacle: The unrestricted P8-free case must be handled without assuming bounded clique number, extra forbidden cycles, or small lists.

tasks.label: 2P4-free graph 3-coloring search
tasks.definition: Input: a simple graph with no induced disjoint union of two four-vertex paths. Return a proper at-most-three coloring, or NO-SOLUTION.
tasks.status: Open in cited sources; no resolution found in scoped search; independent status review pending
tasks.obstacle: The extra C5-free assumption in the known algorithm cannot be silently added.

tasks.label: Diameter-two graph 3-coloring search
tasks.definition: Input: a connected simple graph whose every pair of vertices is at distance at most two. Return a proper at-most-three coloring, or NO-SOLUTION.
tasks.status: Open in cited sources; no resolution found in scoped search; independent status review pending
tasks.obstacle: Existing seed-based branching does not establish a polynomial-size 2-CNF encoding for all diameter-two graphs.

tasks.label: P7-free independent-set threshold search
tasks.definition: Input: a P7-free graph and integer k. Return an independent vertex set of size at least k, or NO-SOLUTION.
tasks.status: Open in cited sources; no resolution found in scoped search; independent status review pending
tasks.obstacle: Do not impose bounded clique number; the known result under that additional promise is insufficient.

tasks.label: Line graph boxicity-at-most-two search
tasks.definition: Input: a simple root graph H and its line graph L(H). Return two rational interval systems whose intersection graph is L(H), or NO-SOLUTION. Endpoint ranks give a finite witness.
tasks.status: Open in cited sources; no resolution found in scoped search; independent status review pending
tasks.obstacle: A two-dimensional representation has interacting interval-order constraints; no polynomial reduction to 2-SAT is supplied by the source.

tasks.label: Line graph interval-completion budget search
tasks.definition: Input: a simple root graph H, its line graph L(H), and integer budget k. Return at most k added edges and an interval representation of the resulting supergraph, or NO-SOLUTION.
tasks.status: Open in cited sources; no resolution found in scoped search; independent status review pending
tasks.obstacle: Optimization on complements is solved in the cited paper, but cannot be reused for line graphs by reversing complementation.

tasks.label: Planar two-bend CPG representation search
tasks.definition: Input: a simple planar graph. Return grid paths with at most two bends, pairwise disjoint interiors, and exactly the prescribed contacts, or NO-SOLUTION. Coordinates use rank compression.
tasks.status: Open in cited sources; no resolution found in scoped search; independent status review pending
tasks.obstacle: The endpoint-forcing gadget suggested in the source is not constructed; witness recovery from the hardness gadget remains a separate obligation.
